name: sdd
description: Spec-Driven Development for Claude Code. It has 22 atomic, stack-agnostic skills and 9 subagents. They carry a feature from idea → spec → design → data-model → API → tasks → tests → implement → review → ship. A TDD implementation engine and a living roadmap sit above the per-feature flow. Start with `survey`: it maps an existing codebase or bootstraps an empty one. Then walk the gated backbone. Each stage reads the previous artifact. It hard-refuses if the artifact is missing. Keep `docs/roadmap.md` (Now/Next/Later, outcome-altitude, never dates) in sync. `specify` promotes a feature to Now. `ship` moves it to Shipped. The Q&A skills are depth-tunable (easy/medium/hard — decide-for-me vs. interrogate-me-with-trade-offs). The ideation analyses run as named subagents (researcher/strategist/analyst/devil's-advocate), gated by that dial. Diagrams are presented in prose and written to file. Raw Mermaid is never dumped to the terminal. Every acceptance criterion is covered end-to-end. design is surface-aware: it declares the feature's target surfaces at the architecture stage (backend-service / web-frontend / mobile-app / desktop-app / cli / worker / library-sdk, each a C4 container). Downstream stages gate their output by that choice: the `ui` task layer, UI-driven sequence flows, and the component / visual-regression / e2e-through-UI frontend test tiers. `ui` work reuses the repo's existing design system (components / tokens / styling) from the architecture map. It never reinvents. Every stage ends with a copy-ready handoff block: what changed, the files to review, then `/clear` + the next `/sdd:…` command. Three skills close the outer loops: `refine` (an optional second pass that re-analyzes the codebase and corrects tasks/*.md + tasks.json atomically), `loop` (a gated, resumable six-phase polish loop over a single artifact), and `evolve` (mines _fixes/ + _review/ records for recurring prevention points and writes project-specific rules to docs/.skill-context/sdd-<skill>/SKILL.md that every skill reads at startup as a project-level override, without ever editing the installed skills).
